open_risks.risk: Reviewers may dismiss the benchmark as only wall-collision detection.
open_risks.mitigation: Frame the task family as metric consequence, configurational comparison, short action simulation, and embodied counterfactual reasoning; report T1/T2/T4 separately and use T3/T5 only after validation.

open_risks.risk: Single-image monocular scale ambiguity could make some labels visually underdetermined.
open_risks.mitigation: Use body-width normalization, discard bin-boundary cases, require visible_sweep_ratio >= 0.7, require collision visibility where relevant, and run human sanity checks.

open_risks.risk: Hidden geometry could turn the benchmark into guessing around corners or behind occluders.
open_risks.mitigation: Core cases must have requires_hidden_geometry=false, fov_supported=true, ambiguous=false, and visible decisive evidence.

open_risks.risk: Language priors, radius priors, answer imbalance, or action priors could explain model performance.
open_risks.mitigation: Use same-image counterfactual groups, balanced labels, blind M5, radius-only/action-only baselines, majority baselines, and geometric heuristics such as center-ray and corridor-width controls.

open_risks.risk: Habitat navmesh labels may not match what is visually legible from RGB.
open_risks.mitigation: Store RGB, depth, top-down, sweep overlay, oracle trace, collision pixel, geometric explanation, and visible evidence notes; manually audit showcase cases before scaling.

open_risks.risk: T4 flip cases may be sparse or too subtle in random samples.
open_risks.mitigation: Run a survey pass over scenes and radii first, then stratified rejection sample around visible bottlenecks while retaining no-flip controls.

open_risks.risk: Prompt wording may leak labels through spatial adjectives.
open_risks.mitigation: Lint templates against banned answer-revealing words and keep scene explanations in display-only fields.

open_risks.risk: If oracle, blind, human, and VLM validity gates do not separate cleanly, the paper claim collapses.
open_risks.mitigation: Treat the demo as a go/no-go probe: stop or redesign if M4 is not high, M5 is not near random, humans do not beat VLMs, or VLMs approach the oracle.

open_risks.risk: These are illustrative cases, not simulator-oracle labels.
open_risks.mitigation: Replace or verify every answer with Habitat swept-cylinder labels once data_manifest.json is available.

open_risks.risk: T3 and T5 are more vulnerable to hidden-geometry ambiguity than T1/T2/T4.
open_risks.mitigation: Only keep T3/T5 cases with fov_supported=true, visible_sweep_ratio>=0.7, and requires_hidden_geometry=false.

open_risks.risk: Some display cases require an indicated local target or direction overlay in the rendered prompt package.
open_risks.mitigation: Ensure the final HTML/data view includes the target/action marker when the question references an indicated target.

open_risks.risk: Published benchmark collapses into visible corridor-width or wall-distance classification rather than body-conditioned swept-volume reasoning.
open_risks.mitigation: Require center-ray, largest-floor-patch, corridor-width, radius-only, action-only, and majority baselines to stay near chance or clearly below M1/humans.

open_risks.risk: Labels disagree with what a single RGB image supports because navmesh collision points are outside view, behind occluders, or created by depth/rendering artifacts.
open_risks.mitigation: Gate every case with saved RGB/depth/topdown/sweep overlay, collision_point_pixel, visible_sweep_ratio, collision_point_visible, requires_hidden_geometry=false, and manual audit.

open_risks.risk: T4 becomes a monotonic-radius quiz instead of an embodied counterfactual test.
open_risks.mitigation: Randomize body A/B order, remove impossible distractors or score against a monotonic prior baseline, specify horizon, and require same-image flip plus no-flip groups.

open_risks.risk: Single-image monocular scale makes T1 bins visually noisy near thresholds.
open_risks.mitigation: Freeze bins only after survey histograms; discard bin_margin_body_widths < 0.5; report human agreement and ordinal off-by-one error.

open_risks.risk: Prompt/template leakage makes M5 non-random.
open_risks.mitigation: Lint prompts for banned geometry words, balance templates, and fail or revise any task where blind M5 exceeds chance by more than a small tolerance.

open_risks.risk: T3 and long-horizon T5 require predicting around turns, outside the FOV, or beyond reliable visible evidence.
open_risks.mitigation: Keep T3/T5 extension-only until fov_supported and visible_sweep_ratio pass on real cases; remove any sample with decisive hidden geometry.

open_risks.risk: Taxonomy may look borrowed from spatial-intelligence benchmarks rather than derived from EgoConseq's formula.
open_risks.mitigation: Name categories directly from swept-volume readouts and cite external taxonomies only as methodological inspiration, not as task definitions.

open_risks.risk: Live pipeline verification is blocked if the Habitat environment, HM3D/MP3D paths, radius-specific navmesh recomputation, or writeable artifact directory are unavailable under --runner codex.
open_risks.mitigation: Start pipeline_verify with a small environment probe that saves RGB, depth, top-down, sweep overlay, oracle trace, and data_manifest entries before generating the full demo.

open_risks.risk: Oracle labels may be wrong if navmesh erosion is double-counted or visibility projection is mishandled.
open_risks.mitigation: Recompute navmesh per radius, use 0.05m stepping, store collision pixels, and manually audit at least 20 probe cases.

open_risks.risk: Illustrative HTML may be mistaken for validated benchmark evidence.
open_risks.mitigation: Add a visible 'illustrative only / not simulator-validated' badge to every non-oracle case and keep empirical claims out of the HTML until pipeline_verify passes.

open_risks.risk: Prompt wording, answer priors, radius-only priors, or center-ray heuristics can create shortcut solutions.
open_risks.mitigation: Run prompt lint, balance answer distributions, and report M5, majority, radius-only, action-only, center-ray, and corridor-width baselines.

open_risks.risk: T3 and T5 can drift into hidden-space inference rather than visible local consequence reasoning.
open_risks.mitigation: Keep them extension-only until visible_sweep_ratio >= 0.7, fov_supported=true, collision evidence visibility, and requires_hidden_geometry=false are verified.

open_risks.risk: Current T4 wording creates a monotonicity shortcut because 'only B' is impossible when Body B is always larger.
open_risks.mitigation: Either remove 'only B' from the answer space or randomize body order and label choices as only smaller / only larger with explicit radius metadata.

motivation: EgoConseq-Bench evaluates whether a vision-language model can infer the visible local physical consequence of its own body executing a short action from one egocentric RGB image. The target is not navigation, object physics, or generic spatial relations; it is body-conditioned ego swept-volume consequence reasoning.

adjudication.rationale: The pipeline probe is verified; run deterministic batch case generation before showcase review.

design_principles: Single-image ego-action VQA: one RGB frame, one body description, one action primitive, one answer.
Body is a query-conditioned causal collision operator: do(body=r) can flip the consequence on the same image.
Distances are body-width normalized, with 1 body-width = 2r, avoiding absolute metric-distance claims from monocular RGB.
Labels come from deterministic swept-cylinder geometry and visibility filtering, not LLM judgment.
Core cases must be visible or directly inferable: no hidden-corner, off-image, or occluded decisive geometry.
Counterfactual body/action pairs, blind controls, option balancing, and shortcut heuristics are mandatory validity checks.
Swept-cylinder collision is the label engine, not the novelty claim; the novelty is the isolated diagnostic of MLLM embodied consequence grounding.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Forward swept-volume extent
inspired_by: EgoConseq swept-volume formula; VSI-Bench / Thinking in Space only as motivation-to-QA methodology inspiration
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Reads out how far the current body can move forward before first visible collision, normalized by body width.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Visible directional swept-volume comparison
inspired_by: EgoConseq action-conditioned visible collision evidence; prior spatial benchmarks only as coverage-design inspiration
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Compares which visible candidate sweep, or fixed visible horizon, remains collision-free for the queried body.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Short action-sequence consequence
inspired_by: MindCube only as what-if QA construction inspiration, not unseen-space reasoning
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Tests a small turn-then-forward consequence while retaining the visible-local swept-volume boundary.

spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.name: Body-intervention consequence
inspired_by: Counterfactual QA methodology only; the intervention is EgoConseq's do(body=r) collision operator
spatial_intelligence_taxonomy.goal_fit: Holds image and action fixed while changing radius to test embodiment-sensitive consequence flips and no-flip controls.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Action: move straight forward. How many body-widths can it move before first contact? Options: <2, 2-4, 4-8, >8.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compute forward max_safe_distance_body_widths on the radius-specific navmesh and bin into <2 / 2-4 / 4-8 / >8; require bin_margin_body_widths >= 0.5.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Candidate directions: left-front {theta} degrees, straight, right-front {theta} degrees. Rank them by maximum distance before first contact, longest to shortest.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compute swept distances for {-theta,0,+theta}, sort descending, and require visible evidence plus a ranking margin sufficient to avoid ties; theta defaults to 30 degrees with 15 degrees allowed.

tasks.question_template: Same RGB and action: move straight forward for {horizon} body-widths. Compare Body A radius {r_a} m and Body B radius {r_b} m, height 1.5 m. Which bodies complete the action without contact? Options use both / only smaller body / neither, unless body order is randomized.
tasks.answer_derivation: At the same pose/action/horizon, compare passability across radius-specific navmeshes; produce flip and no-flip controls with counterfactual_group_id and flip_pair_id.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Compare A) move straight forward and B) rotate {theta} degrees, then move forward. Which action allows more body-widths before first contact? Options: A, B, about the same.
tasks.answer_derivation: Compare straight max distance with turn-then-forward max distance; label about the same only within a fixed tie margin of 0.5 body-width. Extension-only until FOV support is verified.

tasks.question_template: Body: cylinder radius {r} m, height 1.5 m. Action: move forward for {horizon} body-widths within the currently visible region. Is the swept body contact-free? Options: yes, no.
tasks.answer_derivation: Check whether every swept sample through the fixed horizon remains navigable for the radius-specific body. Extension-only until hidden-geometry and shortcut risks are audited.

qa_design.name: Body-Width Forward Horizon
qa_design.question_pattern: Ask how many body widths the queried cylindrical body can move straight forward before first visible contact.

qa_design.name: Visible Directional Sweep Ranking
qa_design.question_pattern: Rank left-front, straight, and right-front swept distances within the current FOV.

qa_design.name: Composite Motion Consequence
qa_design.question_pattern: Compare straight motion with a small turn-then-forward action under the same body constraints.

qa_design.name: Body Counterfactual Sweep
qa_design.question_pattern: Hold RGB and action fixed while changing body radius, then ask which bodies complete the sweep.

qa_design.name: Visible Passability
qa_design.question_pattern: Ask whether a fixed forward swept horizon in the visible region is contact-free for the queried body.

novelty_positioning: EgoConseq is single-frame, ego-body, action-conditioned consequence VQA; it is not route navigation, active exploration, or long-horizon planning.
The benchmark does not claim novel collision geometry; swept-cylinder intersection is the deterministic label engine.
Compared with PhysBench, it asks about the ego body rather than object or scene physics.
Compared with CapNav, it is one-step visible-local consequence reasoning rather than route-level capability-conditioned navigation.
Compared with TouchSafeBench, it uses a hypothetical action from single RGB rather than multi-view/current collision grounding.
Compared with ENACT and EXPLORE-Bench, it isolates body-width swept-volume collision/passability rather than broad affordance or scene-state evolution.
VSI-Bench, Thinking in Space, MindCube, and ESI-Bench are cited only for benchmark-design discipline and adjacent positioning, not for importing their QA categories.
